title: FHFA House Price Index — quarterly index with monthly tables (September 2027 and 2027Q3), 9:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: two FHFA primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 and parsed in full by this session rather than inherited from the sibling ledgers that cite the same documents. (1) fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes) -- its "2027 HPI Release Dates" table, eleventh of twelve dated rows, reads verbatim "Tuesday, November 30 | Quarterly Index (with Monthly Tables) | September 2027 and 2027Q3". (2) The published 2026Q2 report (HTTP 200, 1,522,949 bytes, released 2026-08-25), whose "FHFA HPI Release Dates for 2027" appendix page carries the identical row above the statement "Public FHFA HPI(R) releases occur at 9AM ET and include a press release, tables, figures, and associated data" -- a published document, not a second reading of the same web table, and the source of the 9:00 a.m. ET time. THE EDITION TYPE IS QUOTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the same table marks exactly four 2027 rows quarterly -- February 23, May 25, August 31 and November 30 -- so this is one of the four, and its monthly tables are where the August 2027 figure first published on 2027-10-26 gets its first restatement. All twelve 2027 rows were checked against this chain's rule-derived last Tuesdays and all twelve match; 2027-11-30 is the last Tuesday of November 2027 and a full NYSE session. Filed estimate because a proposal is always estimate by contract, and because this calendar's confirmed-tier prefixes have no member for a federal statistical agency's own posted forward calendar; the page and the report are both primary sources and a published 2027 schedule, which is stronger than the estimate label suggests. Promote on an independent second look by whichever lane takes this id, per the no-self-confirm convention eight sibling lanes have followed. notes: DISCOVERED during the fhfa-hpi-2027-10-26 initial research (2026-09-06), which read the FHFA 2027 release table in full from two primaries. It is proposed because it is the SUCCESSOR EDITION to that print and is directly load-bearing for a forward test the proposer registered: FT-fhfa-hpi-2027-10-26-2 predicts the August 2027 m/m printed on 2027-10-26 is positive, and this release's monthly tables carry the first (Previous Estimate) restatement of that figure. FOUR THINGS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS ID. (1) IT IS A QUARTERLY EDITION, AND THE CHAIN HAS FOUR ALREADY. fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24, fhfa-hpi-2027-02-23 and fhfa-hpi-2027-08-31 are the researched quarterly siblings; read them before re-deriving what a quarterly edition contains. The 2026-10-27 ledger measured that quarterly editions have NEVER collided with an FOMC day one -- 0 of 20 -- against 17 of 48 for monthly editions. (2) NOVEMBER IS THE ONE MONTH THAT STRADDLES THE BLACKOUT BOUNDARY. The proposer measured that the last Tuesday falls inside an FOMC communications blackout 7 of 7 in January, April, July and October, 0 of 7 in seven of the remaining eight, and 1 of 7 in NOVEMBER -- the only partial month. Whether 2027-11-30 is inside one depends on the December 2027 meeting (posted 12-07/08), which the Board calls tentative until the October meeting confirms it. Check it; do not assume it from this note. (3) THE SEASONAL QUESTION IS CLOSED, SO DO NOT RE-OPEN IT AS THOUGH IT WERE OPEN. September is the reference month here, and six reference months have now been tested and refuted -- June, July, August, October, November, December -- with August the widest null at p=0.8982. A seventh refutation is a confirmation of a closed hypothesis, not a finding; the interesting content question on a quarterly edition is the restatement, not the season. (4) THE CLEAN INTRADAY WINDOW NOW EXISTS AND IS DOCUMENTED IN THE PROPOSER'S LEG 2 -- Yahoo 1h bars with includePrePost serve a 09:00-09:30 ET pre-market bar that excludes the 10:00 Conference Board print. Its limits (release day equals last Tuesday 34 of 34; pre-market volume not served; 30m/5m capped at 60 days) are documented there too. Same channel caveat as every FHFA entry: symbols is empty and no house playbook is housing- or macro-keyed. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
